headline_draft: Anthropic ships Claude Code update: skill diagnostics, VS Code workflows, and larger output buffers (Sept 5)
summary: Anthropic released a broad Claude Code update on or around September 5, 2026 focused on production reliability and developer workflow polish. The update includes new policy and skill diagnostics (helping PMs understand which skills will run correctly against their data), larger inline command and task output limits (reducing truncation issues when working with large research files or complex prototypes), smoother prompt and session handling, and improved VS Code integration for users who work inside their IDE. The update also improves model selection, Remote Control reliability, and startup performance while fixing numerous bugs. This release signals that Claude Code is moving from experimental tool to production-ready product development platform.
why_pm: As PMs start using Claude Code to prototype, these reliability and diagnostics improvements matter: you can now validate that your workflows won't fail silently, handle multi-step research synthesis without losing context midway, and integrate seamlessly into the VS Code environment where many product-focused engineers already live. The diagnostics feature is specifically valuable for PMs iterating with non-technical stakeholders.
key_facts: New skill diagnostics help PMs understand what will/won't work before execution
Larger output buffers reduce truncation when synthesizing long documents or research
VS Code workflows improved for IDE-native development
Policy diagnostics embedded for enterprise/compliance checks
Remote Control and startup reliability improved alongside session handling
quotes: Claude Code ships a broad update with new policy and skill diagnostics, larger inline command and task output limits, and smoother prompt and session handling. It also improves VS Code workflows, model selection, Remote Control, and startup reliability while fixing many bugs and performance issues.

headline_draft: BiomX Zorronet: No-Code AI Agents Move Into Physical-World Operations (September 4, 2026)
summary: BiomX's Zorronet launched a no-code visual builder that lets operational teams connect cameras, sensors, drones, and physical systems into autonomous response workflows without programming or developer support. Operators assemble site-specific logic from predefined capability blocks, modify it on screen, and run multiple workflows in parallel. The platform unifies diverse devices into one AI-managed layer that interprets activity, coordinates responses in real time, and can operate autonomously or with human-in-the-loop approvals. This is agentic AI moving from software into the physical world.
why_pm: This shows the PM challenge expanding from digital workflows into physical operations. Expect questions about safety, liability, reversibility, and audit trails. Study Zorronet's approach to operator control, approval gates, and human-in-the-loop design — these patterns will become table stakes for agent products.
key_facts: Launched September 4, 2026 by BiomX (rebranding to Tessera Defense and Homeland Security)
No-code visual builder lets operators design autonomous response workflows without programming
Connects cameras, sensors, drones, gates, and other on-site systems in parallel workflows
Operates autonomously or with human-in-the-loop approvals
Can run on-premises inside hardened networks or through the cloud
Designed for defense, security, critical infrastructure, and municipal operations
quotes: The real value would come not from any single device, but from the ability to understand the full operational picture. Zorronet brings those inputs together through a unified AI/ML autonomous decision layer, allowing the system to understand context, coordinate assets and determine the appropriate response.
Operational teams connect existing cameras, sensors and physical systems into site-specific response logic and change it on screen without code, software releases or developer support.

sources.label: BiomX Zorronet Launches No-Code AI Workflows, September 4, 2026
